commands.install: PY=$(command -v python3.13 || command -v python3.12 || command -v python3.11 || command -v python3); "$PY" -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -e '.[dev]'
commands.run: D=.factory/sandbox/stubs/sandbox-admin; if [ -d .factory/sandbox/stubs/stubs/sandbox-admin ]; then D=.factory/sandbox/stubs/stubs/sandbox-admin; fi; exec .venv/bin/uvicorn --app-dir "$D" sandbox_app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.why: The only variable this repo reads. app/settings.py:18 is the single os.environ call in app/, and tests/conftest.py:16 is the only other one; nothing loads a .env file, which README.md states is deliberate. It points at the throwaway Postgres sidecar declared under services, never at anything real: the app creates its tables at startup and the test suite writes rows, so whatever this names gets written to. 127.0.0.1 is literal rather than 'localhost' as the README and ci.yml use, because localhost can resolve to ::1 where a service bound to 127.0.0.1 does not answer. A role working in a container cannot dial this address itself - only the app's port is bridged in - so the same database is reachable from there over HTTP under /__sandbox; see capabilities.exercised.

services.name: db
services.why: The service cannot start without a database: the FastAPI lifespan in app/main.py:21-23 calls Base.metadata.create_all(), and /health runs a real SELECT 1 through a session, so it answers only when Postgres does. Seven of the eighteen tests (tests/test_api.py) need it. postgres:17-alpine is the image the repo's own compose.yaml and .github/workflows/ci.yml already use. The credentials are the repo's published throwaway ones and the container is started with --rm and no volume, so it holds nothing worth keeping.

dropped.why: That is how compose makes the database throwaway. The sandbox starts the container with `docker run --rm` and no volume, which gets the same result, and the manifest's service schema has no tmpfs field to carry it.

The sandbox's only readiness option is a TCP port check (`ready: port`), and an open port is not proof the database will accept a connection. The test command makes up the difference with a real psycopg connect that retries for 60s, so an unready database fails the step rather than producing a confusing test error.
The sandbox binds the service to 127.0.0.1 only. Nothing outside the sandbox has any business reaching it.

Compose is how a person starts the sidecar on a laptop. The sandbox starts the same postgres:17-alpine image itself from `services`, so the database is declared in one place for the factory rather than two that can drift.

--reload starts a file-watching supervisor that re-execs a child process. The trial stops the app by signalling its process group, and a supervisor makes what is actually running harder to reason about. The sandbox runs one non-reloading process.

That provisions a CI runner's interpreter; the sandbox has no Actions steps. install picks the newest interpreter already present that satisfies requires-python >= 3.11 and builds a venv from it. Measured at setup: 3.13.18.
`localhost` can resolve to ::1, where a service bound to 127.0.0.1 does not answer. The sandbox uses the literal 127.0.0.1 for both DATABASE_URL and app_url.

dropped.what: `pip install -e '.[dev]'` against the runner's system interpreter
dropped.why: setup-python makes that safe in CI. Without it, Ubuntu 24.04 marks its system Python externally managed (PEP 668) and refuses the install. The sandbox uses a venv at .venv/ and calls its binaries by path, so no command depends on which interpreter is first on PATH.

exercised: All four HTTP endpoints against a real PostgreSQL 17: GET /health, POST /readings, GET /readings, GET /sensors/{sensor}/summary.
The whole test suite with the database present - 18 passed, including the 7 in tests/test_api.py that skip when DATABASE_URL is unset. 96% total coverage via pytest-cov.

Reading and writing the sandbox database from a role's own container, over the app's port, which is the only thing bridged in. `run` serves .factory/sandbox/stubs/sandbox-admin/sandbox_app.py: that module is app.main:app itself plus four routes under /__sandbox, every one include_in_schema=False, so /openapi.json and /docs are byte-identical to the unmodified service (compared at setup, identical). From inside a container they are http://host.docker.internal:8787/__sandbox/... ; on the runner, http://127.0.0.1:8000/__sandbox/... .

POST /__sandbox/sql with {"sql": "..."} runs statements against DATABASE_URL and returns their rows as JSON; add {"params": {...}} to bind :name values. Measured at setup: `DELETE FROM readings` reported rowcount 5; a GROUP BY returned both sensors; a three-statement script returned all three result sets; an unknown table came back 400 with psycopg's own UndefinedTable message rather than a bare 500.

States the HTTP API cannot construct are reachable through that endpoint and are then visible to the real API: a row with recorded_at backdated to 2019 and celsius -300 (below the -273.15 floor ReadingIn enforces) was inserted and came back from GET /readings?sensor=attic.

POST /__sandbox/seed applies the same five rows as the `seed` command - one definition, SEED_ROWS in sandbox_seed.py, which the command runs as a script and the route imports, so they cannot drift. POST /__sandbox/reset empties readings and restarts its id sequence, so reset-then-seed gives ids 1..5 every time and an acceptance check may name one. Measured at setup: reset {"deleted": 6}, seed {"seeded": 5}, then GET /sensors/kitchen/summary returned count 3, min 19.0, max 23.25, mean 21.25.
Table creation from app/models.py by Base.metadata.create_all() in the FastAPI startup lifespan.
SQLAlchemy ORM reads and writes through app/db.py's session() context manager, including its commit-on-success and rollback-on-exception path.
Pydantic validation at the edge: 422 for a reading below -273.15C or above 1000C, and for an empty sensor name.
The 404 for a sensor with no readings, rather than a summary of zeros (app/summary.py:14 raising, app/main.py:72 translating).
/health as a genuine readiness check: it executes SELECT 1 through a session, so it fails when the database is gone.

ruff check . and mypy app under strict = true, the two static checks CI runs before pytest. ruff lints .factory/sandbox/stubs/ too, since those files are committed; both modules are clean under the repo's own rule set.
The rendered Swagger UI at http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in a real browser - all four operations and all five schemas, captured as a full-page screenshot, with the /__sandbox routes absent from it.

not_exercised.what: Schema migrations, and any change to an existing table that already holds rows.
not_exercised.why: There is no migration tool in this repo - no alembic/ directory and nothing in pyproject.toml's dependencies. The app calls Base.metadata.create_all(), which creates tables that do not exist and never alters one that does. The sandbox's database is empty at every start, so a column change that would break a populated table passes here. POST /__sandbox/sql can now put rows in before the change and read them after, which makes such a break visible if a check thinks to look; it does not make it fail on its own.

not_exercised.what: Durability: data surviving a restart, retention, or backup.
not_exercised.why: The sidecar runs from `docker run --rm` with no volume, so every run starts with an empty database. Nothing here can tell a change that preserves data from one that silently discards it.

The engine's pool_pre_ping (app/db.py:19) and the module-level engine and sessionmaker singletons are only ever driven one request at a time here. Pool exhaustion, a session leaking across requests, and reconnecting after the database drops a connection are all unreached. /__sandbox/sql shares that one engine, so it cannot be used to force contention either.

not_exercised.what: How the database connection is secured - TLS, sslmode, or any credential handling.
not_exercised.why: DATABASE_URL points at a throwaway Postgres over loopback with a published password and no sslmode. A change to how the connection string is built, or to what the app does when a credential is absent, has no realistic case here.

not_exercised.what: Any PostgreSQL version, extension or configuration other than postgres:17-alpine's defaults.
not_exercised.why: The sandbox pins the image the repo's own compose.yaml and CI use. What the owner actually runs is not recorded anywhere in this repo, so version-specific SQL or a dependency on an extension would pass here and fail there. Setup itself could not run Docker, so every measurement below was taken against the PostgreSQL 18.7 server installed in the setup agent's own machine, with the same throwaway user, password and database name.

not_exercised.what: Anything that needs a port other than the app's from inside a role's container - a psql shell, a database GUI, a second service.
not_exercised.why: bsf forwards exactly one port to the container: the one in app_url, published as host.docker.internal:8787 (serveOnHost in the runner). There is no manifest field for a second one. /__sandbox is the whole of what this amendment could add - SQL over HTTP, not a connection. A role needing a real psql session, a protocol-level test, or COPY FROM a local file still cannot have one here.

Amendment fe3d81f91d435c56. The verifier reported that it could reach neither the database at DATABASE_URL nor the manifest's `seed` command from its container. Read the runner's own code to find what a container actually gets, rather than guessing at it: serveOnHost in bsf.mjs, and schema/sandbox.json for what the manifest may declare.
episode.observed: serveOnHost takes the port out of app_url, starts one TCP forwarder on 0.0.0.0:8787 pointing at it, and writes /tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/app.json. That is the only bridge. Services are started with -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>, which a container cannot reach, and the manifest schema has no field for exposing a second port. So the report is right and no combination of services, egress or env fixes it.
episode.changed: Settled on carrying database access over the one port that does get through, rather than looking for a second one.

episode.tried: Two ways to put admin routes on that port. First a stdlib reverse proxy on 8000 forwarding to uvicorn on 8001 and answering /__sandbox itself. Then, instead, an ASGI module that imports app.main:app and adds the routes to that same FastAPI instance.
episode.observed: The proxy means two processes, a second port, a 502 window while uvicorn starts, and a hand-written HTTP implementation between the verifier and the app it is verifying. The ASGI module is one process on one port and no proxy; the only question it raises is whether it changes what the app looks like.
episode.changed: Dropped the proxy. Wrote .factory/sandbox/stubs/sandbox-admin/sandbox_app.py, which is `from app.main import app` plus four routes under /__sandbox, each marked include_in_schema=False. `run` serves it with uvicorn --app-dir, so the repo is untouched and the module ships with the sandbox.

episode.tried: Checked the thing that would make that trade bad: whether the added routes change the app under verification. Fetched /openapi.json from the served module and compared it with app.main:app's own app.openapi(), then opened /docs in a real browser.
episode.observed: The two documents are identical. /openapi.json lists /health, /readings and /sensors/{sensor}/summary and contains no occurrence of the string __sandbox. Swagger UI rendered the same four operations and five schemas as before the amendment, with the same single console error - the favicon at fastapi.tiangolo.com, blocked by this agent's firewall.
episode.changed: Nothing. Kept tier `renders` and app_url as they were.

episode.observed: reset {"deleted": 6}; seed {"seeded": 5, "sensors": ["garage", "kitchen"]}; GROUP BY returned both sensors with their counts; DELETE FROM readings returned rowcount 5 and GET /sensors/kitchen/summary then 404; the backdated row (recorded_at 2019-03-01, celsius -300, which ReadingIn rejects with a 422) came back from GET /readings?sensor=attic.
